name: Institutional change

subjectOf.text: Large decentralized networks such as national democracies do not make fundamental changes easily, because stability is their primary quality.
subjectOf.abstract: Large decentralized networks, like national democracies, don't make fundamental changes easily. Stability is their pri- mary quality.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Introduction to Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782192
scope_conditions: large decentralized networks such as national democracies

subjectOf.text: Path dependencies are a major obstacle to decentralizing institutions and businesses, because humans have psychological inertia and cling to familiar systems, especially those that have given them comfort in the past.
subjectOf.abstract: Path dependencies create a major obstacle to decentralizing our institutions and businesses. Humans have psychological inertia, and cling to any familiar system, but especially those that have given them comfort in the past.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Future of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782201

subjectOf.text: Path dependent institutional lock in loses its grip when agents can simulate the long run consequences of alternative institutional trajectories and migrate instantaneously to superior equilibria.
subjectOf.abstract: path-dependent lock-in effects—historically the most persistent source of institutional rigidity—lose their grip when agents can simulate the long-run consequences of alternative institutional trajectories and migrate instantaneously to superior equilibria
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The AI-to-AI Economy and the Collapse of Anthropocentric Economic Theory (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5886442
scope_conditions: assumes agents can simulate and evaluate institutional trajectories at negligible cost
